messages:
incident-bot: [P1] GPU pool us-west-2-gpu-4 at 97% capacity. Autoscaler failed to create new MIG slices due to placement constraints. Queue length rising: 12,400 requests. Paging on-call.

oncall_sre_jordan: I'm on pager. Pulling autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated errors: "no compatible node for slice request: requested_mig_sizes=[1xA100-40Gi, 2xA100-20Gi] available_slots=[3xA100-20Gi, leftover=40Gi]"

nate-eng-runtime: That error matches previous fragmentation pattern — MIG leftover prevents packing. Likely recent workload shift increased 40Gi reqs. Suggest temporary mitigation: allow mixing MIG sizes or permit degraded placement to spill to spare pool.

kevin: Running diagnostics:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=us-west-2-gpu-4 -o wide
kubectl describe node gpu-node-371
kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler -n infra | tail -n 200
```
Initial output: 24 nodes, 8 nodes with 40Gi slices, 16 nodes with 20Gi slices. Autoscaler rejects because it tries to place 40Gi on 20Gi nodes.

lucy-product: CS alert: 503s for some customers on /v1/generate. High priority accounts affected: Acme Inc, ParcelX. Customers seeing timeouts after 20s and 5xx error spikes. We're preparing status page; ETA to notify 10m.

ajay-eng-infra: Proposed live mitigations:
- increase autoscaler max_instances from 120 -> 160 (allows spawn of new nodes while we rebalance)
- force manual rebalance to consolidate 40Gi slices: `allocator rebalance --pool us-west-2-gpu-4 --target-mig 40Gi --strategy greedy --force`
- temporarily lower min_mig_of_type(40Gi) to 0 to allow packing.
I'll open PR to patch autoscaler flags and hotpatch the controller.

kevin: I'm running allocator rebalance now (manual). Monitoring queue.

ops-bot: Command accepted: `allocator rebalance` initiated by kevin at 2026-03-15T04:08:12Z. Steps: draining nodes with small MIGs, consolidate large jobs.

kevin: Rebalance step 1 complete — moved 6 heavy pods onto 3 40Gi nodes, freed up 4 nodes with mixed small slices.

nate-eng-runtime: Also patching runtime to accept cross-slice placement for warmable tasks (best-effort fallback) — risk: potential increased latency. Rolling to 5% canary.

sara-cs: Notified Acme and ParcelX via email and posted status page: "We are experiencing degraded GPU capacity in us-west-2. We are actively mitigating. Some requests may return 503s or experience higher latency."

kevin: Autoscaler max_instances patched to 160 at 04:12 UTC. New nodes coming up. Queue length: 12,400 -> 6,200.

oncall_sre_jordan: Handoff to ajay at 04:15 UTC. I'm stepping off pager; leave alerts to on-call.

ajay-eng-infra: Taking over. Running `kubectl get pods -n workloads --sort-by=.status.startTime` to identify heavy pods. Also increasing `burst_capacity` flag.

ajay-eng-infra: Manual rebalance + scale up completed at 04:22 UTC. Freed 8 GPUs equivalent capacity. Queue drained to 900 in 12m. 5xx rate back to baseline for most customers, Acme still reporting intermittent failures.

lucy-product: Customer impact summary: ~37 minutes of intermittent 503/timeout for top-10 tenants. Estimated affected requests: ~45k. CS outbound: Acme (high touch) follow-up scheduled.

kevin: Rolling autoscaler config change to main: raise max_instances permanently, add condition to prefer binpack with mixed-mig-aware algorithm. PR #8456

nate-eng-runtime: Post-incident follow-ups:
- implement better predictive packing heuristics
- add metric: mig_fragmentation_ratio and alert when >0.25
- add autoscaler fallback to spin spare nodes with permissive MIG composition

sara-cs: Status update posted. Customers notified. Sending proactive credits to Acme.

lucy-product: Postmortem owner: lucy-product. Target due date: 2026-03-22. Action items assigned to kevin, ajay, nate.

oncall_sre_jordan: Closing handoff. If anything recurs, re-open incident thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 2026-03-15T04:35:01Z — pool capacity restored, autoscaler healthy. Tags: gpu, autoscale, mig-fragmentation, customer-impact
